positioning: A versioned operational crosswalk to the bundled partner quality bar. Baseline obligations and unapproved operational extensions are distinct. Structural validation is not certification or Microsoft approval.

core.name: Canonical partner requirements (121 IDs; 60 package/conditional and 61 component rows)

requirements.requirement: Uses an OSI-approved, non-copyleft license.
Public source repository for shipped versions.
All direct and transitive dependencies use OSI-approved, non-copyleft licenses.
Required third-party license and notice files are preserved.
NuGet `PackageLicenseExpression` is populated.
NuGet `RepositoryUrl` is populated.
NuGet `RepositoryCommit` identifies the commit SHA.
NuGet `Authors` is populated.
NuGet `ProjectUrl` is populated.
Every packaged binary is attributable to public partner source or a referenced NuGet/npm package with a clear upstream; released partner binaries map to the public source commit.
Every shipped assembly is strong-name signed.
Every shipped assembly is Authenticode-signed using the partner's verified publisher identity.
Every shipped .nupkg is NuGet-signed for package integrity.
NuGet.org repository signature is present where expected.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: A separate repository-signature expectation exceeds the baseline requirement for NuGet signing.

requirements.requirement: OIDC/trusted publishing is used instead of long-lived publish secrets.
An SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM is published with every release.
The SBOM enumerates direct and transitive dependencies.
Bundled third-party JS/CSS upstream components and versions are listed in the SBOM.
Required bundled third-party license and notice files are preserved.
SBOM and provenance bind to the exact final signed NuGet package digest.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Exact final-package digest binding is a stronger audit protocol, not an explicit baseline SBOM delivery obligation.

requirements.requirement: Build provenance connects source SHA, workflow, dependencies, signatures, and publication.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: End-to-end workflow provenance is stronger than the baseline binary-attribution requirement.

requirements.requirement: Release evidence is retained long enough for validation and incident response.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Evidence retention duration is an operational policy not specified in the baseline.

requirements.requirement: Maintain a documented security/threat model for the library.
Complete a library security review before shipping.
Address all identified threats and review findings, or explicitly accept them with documented justification before release.
Publish SECURITY.md with a private disclosure contact.
Vulnerabilities are reported and fixed privately and disclosed only after a fix is available.
Dependency vulnerability scanning runs on every release; PR scanning is optional.
Do not ship known unpatched High/Critical CVEs in any direct or transitive dependency.
Ship vulnerability fixes in line with .NET servicing, typically the next monthly Patch Tuesday after a fix is ready.
Consider an out-of-band release for critical issues with known exploitation.
No default phone-home behavior, telemetry, or remote script/style/font loading.
Any telemetry is opt-in and documented.
Review and apply Blazor static SSR and Interactive Server threat-mitigation guidance.
Browser event/input values are not represented as server authorization evidence.
All interactive components conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA in their default configuration.
No known AA failures at ship.
Accessibility Insights for Web FastPass is clean on a representative sample app for every release.
At least one full Accessibility Insights Assessment is completed per major release.
Each major release is smoke-tested with NVDA, JAWS, or Windows Narrator.
Keyboard-only operation is verified.
Focus order, trapping, restoration, and visible focus are verified where applicable.
Semantic roles, names, values, states, and relationships are correct.
Screen-reader smoke testing confirms selection, expansion, validation, and async-load announcements.
Components remain usable in Windows High Contrast and CSS forced-colors mode.
All user-visible strings are localizable.
Record RTL support when claimed; RTL is optional, not a promotion gate.
Support the latest stable .NET on GA day; earlier .NET support is allowed but not required.
Document supported static SSR, Interactive Server, Interactive WebAssembly, and Auto modes.
Clearly document supported modes and give a clear compile-time or runtime error in unsupported modes.
Prerendering must not throw.
Static SSR output has a documented usefulness/accessibility contract.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: A separate documented SSR usefulness contract exceeds correct operation or explicit unsupported-mode handling.

requirements.requirement: Interactive Server works correctly when supported.
Interactive WebAssembly works correctly when supported.
Auto transition behavior works correctly when supported.
Use [Parameter] { get; set; } auto-properties; no required/init (BL0007) and no internal parameter mutation.
Use [EditorRequired] where appropriate.
Use EventCallback/EventCallback<T>, not Action/Func, for component events.
Observe callback tasks and route fire-and-forget errors through ComponentBase.DispatchExceptionAsync.
Use InvokeAsync + StateHasChanged for external events.
No .Result, .Wait(), Task.Run, ContinueWith, or Thread.Start on the renderer sync context.
Clean up subscriptions, timers, CancellationTokenSource, IJSObjectReference and DotNetObjectReference instances; catch JSDisconnectedException when disposing JS references.
Components owning subscriptions, timers, CancellationTokenSource, or JS references implement IAsyncDisposable.
Use collocated .razor.js ES modules loaded from OnAfterRenderAsync; dispose IJSObjectReference and DotNetObjectReference instances.
No JS interop in OnInitializedAsync.
Serialization is typed and correctly escapes untrusted values.
Use .razor.css for component styles, avoid inline style attributes, and document and prefix any global CSS surface.
Library code builds with no new .NET or Blazor BL* analyzer warnings on supported TFMs; an accepted migration plan is not a substitute.
XML documentation comments cover all public APIs.
A public documentation site provides samples for each component covering all supported render modes.
Follow SemVer, mark experimental APIs [Experimental], and ship [Obsolete] guidance for at least one minor version before removal.

Prepare for trimming with <IsTrimmable>true</IsTrimmable>; package-based Interactive WebAssembly trimmed publish succeeds, with a trimmable WASM surface and no large transitive dependencies bloating published apps.
Annotate or fix trim and AOT warnings rather than suppressing them.
The trimmed artifact passes a browser/runtime smoke test.
Annotate reflection/dynamic code with appropriate trimming and AOT attributes.
Interactive WebAssembly AOT compilation succeeds cleanly; absence of a vendor AOT claim does not waive the obligation.
The AOT-compiled WebAssembly artifact passes a runtime smoke test.
The supported trim/AOT matrix is documented.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: A separately published trim/AOT matrix is additional operational documentation, not a baseline exemption from trimming/AOT.

requirements.requirement: Minimize render work: override ShouldRender where appropriate, avoid unnecessary StateHasChanged calls, keep render trees small, and avoid unchanged-result rerenders.
Use @key on lists and repeated elements to preserve identity and avoid unnecessary teardown.
Avoid heavy OnParametersSet/render work; move expensive computation to async lifecycle methods or memoize it.
Virtualize large lists with <Virtualize> or document how consumers can virtualize the content.
Scope cascading values narrowly or use IsFixed="true" when the value does not change.
Keep Interactive Server per-component state small and avoid holding large object graphs in fields.
Server-to-browser payload size, allocation, and copy costs are understood.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Payload/allocation/copy measurements go beyond the baseline per-circuit state guidance.

requirements.requirement: WASM dependency and bundle size are measured against a budget.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: An explicit measured budget is stronger than keeping the WASM surface trimmable and avoiding bloated dependencies. The baseline obligation still applies independently.

requirements.requirement: Startup, render, interaction, and large-data targets are documented.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Published performance targets are not specified in the baseline.

requirements.requirement: Measurements cover supported representative scenarios.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: A representative benchmark evidence matrix is additional operational validation, not a baseline deliverable.

requirements.requirement: PR CI restores, builds, tests, and packages relevant targets.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Mandatory PR build/test/package CI is not specified by the baseline release recheck obligation.

requirements.requirement: Deterministic regression tests cover every accepted product defect.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Per-defect deterministic regression coverage is an additional operational policy.

requirements.requirement: Browser tests cover claimed render modes and JS behavior.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Automated browser-test infrastructure is stronger than the baseline correct-operation requirement.

requirements.requirement: Accessibility smoke tests run at the agreed cadence.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Additional CI cadence requires agreement and does not replace Accessibility Insights FastPass each release or Assessment each major release.

requirements.requirement: Dependency scans and release checks are required gates.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Enforced CI gates are an implementation policy beyond running release scans and not shipping High/Critical CVEs.

requirements.requirement: Default and release refs require appropriate review/checks.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Branch protection and review rules are not specified in the baseline.

requirements.requirement: Untrusted build execution is separated from privileged signing/publishing.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Privilege-separated build architecture is an additional supply-chain control.

requirements.requirement: Signing/publishing consumes a verified immutable artifact.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Immutable artifact promotion is an additional supply-chain control.

requirements.requirement: Documentation examples compile and assert behavior, not only syntax.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Executable behavior assertions for documentation are additional validation beyond public samples.

requirements.requirement: Node, .NET, browser, and workload prerequisites are correct.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: Reproducible probe prerequisite declarations are an audit protocol, not an independent baseline product defect.

requirements.requirement: Release validation rechecks every applicable requirement.
Identify an active maintainer providing timely security, accessibility, and engineering support.
Publish a single support point of contact.
Publish a stated response SLA.
Supported versions are documented.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: A separate supported-version matrix is additional operational documentation.

requirements.requirement: Security patch cadence is documented.
requirements.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: A separately published servicing-cadence policy is stronger than shipping vulnerability fixes on the baseline cadence. The actual servicing obligation remains under SEC-08.

requirements.requirement: Publicly provide sufficient advance EOL notice for customer migrations and Microsoft promotion removal.
Track non-security accessibility bugs and other shipped-version issues publicly.
Use coordinated disclosure for security issues; do not disclose publicly until a fix is available.
Reverify requirements for every release.
Microsoft may stop promoting a partner library if it no longer adheres to these requirements.
In-scope scaffolders integrate with dotnet scaffold, not dotnet new, and are contributed to dotnet/scaffolding under its quality bar.
Generated code follows the accessibility and Blazor patterns in sections 3 and 4.
Generated dependencies are limited to .NET and qualifying partner libraries, with no proprietary or closed-source dependencies.
Generated projects use signed nuget.org packages, no preview-only/internal/non-public feeds, and pinned partner versions.
No execution of arbitrary scripts during scaffolding.
Update scaffolders when library patches or updates affect generated output.
Contribute partner AI skills to the dotnet-blazor plugin in dotnet/skills.
Meet dotnet/skills contribution guidance for format, evals, and ownership.
Update skills for accuracy on each .NET release day and promptly when partner-library changes affect recommended patterns.
Generated code depends only on .NET and qualifying partner libraries.
Generated code does not depend on proprietary or closed-source libraries.
New AI skills complete Responsible AI (RAI) review before merge.

extensions.requirement: Retain a separately recorded package-level trim-analysis opt-in or equivalent-configuration audit.
extensions.extension_basis: operational-2.0.0: TA-08 is not a canonical checklist ID. Its old equivalent-configuration allowance does not replace the baseline IsTrimmable obligation, now explicitly assessed under TA-01. Any extra package-level audit needs policy approval.
